profile.name: Junlin Wu
profile.title: AI Engineer · LLM Inference & Agent Development
profile.bio: Currently at Huawei, owning the quantization and adaptation of multimodal diffusion models and LLMs on Ascend chips. I enjoy bridging RAG, ReAct agents, and low-level inference optimization into verifiable, reusable engineering pipelines.

education.degree: M.S. in Data Science · Focus: Generative AI & LLM Applications
B.S. in Data Science · Minor in Economics · GPA 3.9/4.0 · Cum Laude

desc: Led quantization and precision tuning of Flux, Wan 2.2, and HunYuan multimodal diffusion models on next-gen Ascend chips — Wan 2.2 / HunYuan reached 1.5×, Flux exceeded the 2× target.
As model owner, drove end-to-end adaptation of Qwen3.5 on the new chip in vLLM: functional bring-up, quantization, fused operators, PD-disaggregation, and performance tuning.
Contributed MXFP4/MXFP8 quantization support to SGLang across Diffusion / Dense LLM / MoE scenarios — delivered in ~1 week with AI-assisted coding, vs the originally-scoped 2 months.
Built a pandas-based automated DiT-block profiling tool, saving ~50% analysis time and adopted as a team-wide standard benefiting 5+ projects.

work.company: Columbia University Medical Center · Nectow Lab
desc: Designed an end-to-end analysis pipeline for in-vivo neuronal recordings: denoising, spike detection, and time alignment.
Used statistical modeling to quantify temporal links between neural activity and feeding behavior, helping identify key neuropeptidergic neurons that regulate satiation.
Co-authored work supporting the paper 'Brainstem neuropeptidergic neurons link a neurohumoral axis to satiation' (Cell, under review).
Built the organization's website with Vue.js, Vite, and Flask, plus an internal knowledge-sharing portal for the dev team.
Created programming tutorials for 15 team members and organized academic seminars and major events including the Spring Festival Gala.
